# @aganitha/atk-ui

> Aganitha's shared UI layer: a Web Awesome theme, a small catalog of custom
> elements and patterns, and support for project-local components.

## Install

```bash
npm install @aganitha/atk-ui @awesome.me/webawesome lit
```

Load Web Awesome's theme before atk-ui's theme and add `atk-theme` to the
document root:

```ts
import "@awesome.me/webawesome/dist/styles/themes/default.css";
import "@aganitha/atk-ui/theme.css";
import "@aganitha/atk-ui/patterns.css";
```

```html
<html class="wa-theme-default atk-theme"></html>
```

## API

`AganithaComponent extends LitElement`
  Base class for project-local and shared atk-ui custom elements. Set `static
  css` rather than Lit's `styles` so the common host styles remain active.

`define(tag: string, ctor: CustomElementConstructor): void`
  Registers a custom element when running in a browser. It is a no-op during
  server rendering and when the tag was already registered.

`<atk-metric>`
  Displays one labeled measurement with optional historical values and normal
  range. Import with `@aganitha/atk-ui/components/metric`.

`<atk-go-ribbon>`
  Displays a Gene Ontology ribbon through its maintained upstream component.
  Import with `@aganitha/atk-ui/components/go-ribbon`.

## Examples

```ts
import "@aganitha/atk-ui/components/metric";
```

```html
<atk-metric label="Hemoglobin" value="10.2" unit="g/dL" low="13.5" high="17.5">
  <script type="application/json">[11.8, 11.2, 10.9, 10.4, 10.2]</script>
</atk-metric>
```

For the generated component catalog and usage guidance, install the `atk-ui`
skill pack from this repository.
